sites.name: Harrat Khaybar — Umm Jirsan
sites.fact: Arabia's longest surveyed lava tube: 1,481 m in three sections, inside a vast basaltic lava field.
sites.strong: A real basaltic lava tube, like the cave skylights seen in lunar and Martian lava fields, set in a hyper-arid climate.
sites.weak: Far too warm compared with the Moon or Mars, and the cave holds modern animal and human deposits.
sites.use: Testing cave-exploring robots, GPS-free navigation, and measuring a cave's thermal shielding for sub-surface habitats.
src: Pint, Umm Jirsan: Arabia's longest lava-tube system
sites.kind: Lava tube in a basalt field

sites.name: Harrat Rahat — 1256 CE flow
sites.fact: Saudi Arabia's largest lava field (20,000 km²). The 1256 CE flow travelled 23 km, stopping 4 km from Madinah.
sites.strong: Very young, barely eroded basalt flows and scoria cones, like lunar maria and the Tharsis plains on Mars.
sites.weak: No impact craters; temperature and humidity are much higher.
sites.use: Calibrating satellite views of basalt flows and testing rover mobility over rough lava.

sites.name: Al Wahbah Crater — Harrat Kishb
sites.fact: A volcanic maar about 2.2–2.3 km wide and ~250 m deep, its floor covered by white salts.
sites.strong: A deep crater with a salt floor combines volcanism and evaporation — a mix that echoes salt and sulfate deposits in Martian craters.
sites.weak: Not an impact crater, and its salts come from modern groundwater.
sites.use: Rehearsing sampling on a steep crater floor and studying how salts preserve biosignatures.
src: Moufti et al. 2013 — Geoheritage of Al Wahbah

sites.name: Wabar Craters — Rub' al Khali
sites.fact: A cluster of small, very young impact craters, about 64–116 m across, in the Empty Quarter's sand sea.
sites.strong: Real impact craters with impact glass, being buried by active dunes much like dune-filled Martian craters.
sites.weak: Tiny compared with lunar craters, and formed in sand rather than rock.
sites.use: Studying dune–crater interaction and testing ground-penetrating radar beneath sand.
src: Hanafy et al. 2021 — Geophysical study at Wabar
sites.kind: Impact craters in a sand sea

sites.name: Lonar Crater
sites.fact: An impact crater about 1.8 km across, cut into Deccan basalt and holding a saline, alkaline lake.
sites.strong: One of the rare impact craters in basalt — the rock of the lunar maria and most of Mars.
sites.weak: Humid and vegetated because of the monsoon.
sites.use: Understanding shocked basalt and identifying shocked minerals in lunar samples.

sites.name: Dasht-e Lut — Kaluts
sites.fact: Among the hottest land surfaces measured by satellite, with vast fields of wind-carved yardangs.
sites.strong: Yardangs are among the clearest wind landforms on Mars, as in the Medusae Fossae Formation.
sites.weak: Extremely hot, while Mars is cold.
sites.use: Linking wind speed to erosion rates and testing surface-age models.

sites.name: Dallol — Danakil Depression
sites.fact: A hyper-acidic, hyper-saline hydrothermal system studied as a limit for life.
sites.strong: Acidic brines with sulfate and iron deposits, like ancient water environments on Mars.
sites.weak: Active volcanism; MERRA-2 data at ~0.5° also blends in wetter highlands nearby.
sites.use: Testing life-detection instruments in extreme conditions.

sites.name: Río Tinto
sites.fact: An acidic, iron-rich river with jarosite — the same mineral Opportunity found at Meridiani Planum.
sites.strong: The strongest known analog for the acidic water chemistry of Meridiani on Mars.
sites.weak: Abundant liquid water and a Mediterranean climate.
sites.use: NASA's MARTE drilling project for subsurface life, and calibrating sulfate spectra.

sites.name: Pilbara — Dresser Formation
sites.fact: Holds some of Earth's oldest evidence of life — stromatolites about 3.48 billion years old.
sites.strong: Rocks as old as Mars's wet era, with preserved biosignatures.
sites.weak: A long tectonic and geological history has altered the rocks.
sites.use: Training to recognise ancient biosignatures, as in Perseverance's samples.

sites.name: Qaidam Basin — Dalangtan
sites.fact: A high, cold, very dry basin with dry lakes, salt deposits and yardangs.
sites.strong: Combines cold, altitude, aridity, salts and wind — a rare, Mars-like mix.
sites.use: Studying the salt sequence as lakes dry out, as happened in Gale Crater.

sites.name: Craters of the Moon
sites.fact: A basaltic lava field with tubes and caves where Apollo astronauts trained.
sites.strong: Accessible lava tubes and fresh basalt flows.
sites.weak: Winter snow and high humidity; not dry.
sites.use: NASA cave-exploration programmes and lunar cave modelling.

sites.name: Atacama — Yungay
sites.fact: One of the driest places on Earth, with perchlorates in the soil as on Mars. (Well-known reference analog)
sites.strong: Aridity, salts and almost no life.

sites.name: Haughton Crater
sites.fact: A ~23 km impact crater in the Arctic, home of NASA's Haughton-Mars Project. (Well-known reference analog)

sites.name: McMurdo Dry Valleys
sites.fact: The coldest, driest ice-free place on Earth. (Well-known reference analog)
sites.strong: Cold, dry and ground ice — the closest climate match to Mars.
sites.use: Studying ground ice and microbes living inside rocks.

sites.name: Holuhraun
sites.fact: A basalt lava field formed in 2014–2015 next to a glacier. (Well-known reference analog)

sites.name: Death Valley
sites.fact: Salt flats, dunes and the Ubehebe volcanic crater. (Well-known reference analog)
sites.strong: Salts, dry ancient lakes and wind.

targets.name: Shackleton Crater — South Pole
targets.desc: Its floor lies in permanent shadow while its rim gets near-constant sunlight. The best-known proposed site for a permanent lunar base.

targets.name: Peak near Cabeus B
targets.desc: In Cabeus crater, NASA's LCROSS impactor confirmed water ice in 2009. Coordinates are Cabeus's centre (approximate).

targets.name: Haworth
targets.desc: An old crater with extensive permanent shadow; an Artemis III candidate region.

targets.name: Malapert Massif
targets.desc: High ground with long illumination and direct line-of-sight to Earth. Coordinates are Malapert crater's centre.

targets.name: Mons Mouton & Plateau
targets.desc: A relatively flat high plateau near the pole — two of the nine Artemis III regions.

targets.name: Nobile Rim
targets.desc: The rim of Nobile crater, also the planned target of the VIPER ice-prospecting rover.

targets.name: de Gerlache Rim
targets.desc: A deep crater near the pole with a very cold floor and a sunlit rim.

targets.name: Slater Plain
targets.desc: Added to the Artemis III list in 2024. Coordinates are Slater crater's centre.

targets.name: Marius Hills skylight
targets.desc: An opening in the roof of a basaltic lava tube; a candidate natural shelter from radiation and temperature swings.

targets.name: Mare Tranquillitatis pit
targets.desc: A vertical-walled pit leading to a sub-surface void, confirmed by radar in 2024.

targets.name: Mare Ingenii pit
targets.desc: A cave skylight in a basaltic mare on the lunar far side.

targets.name: Aristarchus pits
targets.desc: Pits in impact melt inside Aristarchus crater, next to a plateau rich in volcanic deposits.

targets.name: Apollo 11 — Sea of Tranquility
targets.desc: First human landing (1969) on a flat basaltic plain.

targets.name: Apollo 12 — Ocean of Storms
targets.desc: Pinpoint landing near Surveyor 3 on mare basalt.

targets.name: Apollo 14 — Fra Mauro
targets.desc: Ejecta from the Imbrium impact basin; breccia rocks.

targets.name: Apollo 15 — Hadley Rille
targets.desc: A sinuous rille — a collapsed lava channel or tube — beside the Apennine mountains.

targets.name: Apollo 16 — Descartes Highlands
targets.desc: The only landing in the bright lunar highlands (anorthosite).

targets.name: Apollo 17 — Taurus-Littrow
targets.desc: A mountain valley with basalt and explosive volcanic deposits (the orange soil).

targets.name: Chang'e 4 — Von Kármán
targets.desc: First far-side landing, inside the giant South Pole–Aitken impact basin.

targets.name: Chang'e 5 — Mons Rümker
targets.desc: Returned samples of the youngest lunar basalt (~2 billion years).

targets.name: Chang'e 6 — Apollo Basin
targets.desc: First far-side samples (2024), from inside an impact basin.

targets.name: Chandrayaan-3
targets.desc: The closest successful landing to the south pole (2023), on ancient highlands.

targets.name: Jezero Crater — Perseverance
targets.desc: An ancient lake with a river delta and carbonates, where Perseverance collects samples to search for signs of life.

targets.name: Gale Crater — Curiosity
targets.desc: Layers of clay and sulfate recording a lake drying out, with the active Bagnold dunes.

targets.name: Meridiani Planum — Opportunity
targets.desc: Jarosite and hematite spherules pointing to ancient acidic water.

targets.name: Gusev Crater — Spirit
targets.desc: Basalt plains, with silica deposits in the Columbia Hills resembling hot-spring deposits.

targets.name: Nili Fossae
targets.desc: Olivine, carbonates and clays — evidence of water reacting with igneous rock. A former Perseverance candidate.

targets.name: Mawrth Vallis
targets.desc: One of the richest regions on Mars for water-formed clay minerals.

targets.name: Oxia Planum — Rosalind Franklin
targets.desc: Landing site of ESA's Rosalind Franklin rover: ancient clays with a sedimentary fan.

targets.name: Eberswalde Crater
targets.desc: A well-preserved meandering delta — among the strongest evidence of flowing water.

targets.name: Columbus Crater
targets.desc: Rings of sulfates and clays inside a crater — remains of a groundwater-fed lake.

targets.name: Melas Chasma — Valles Marineris
targets.desc: Part of the largest canyon in the Solar System, with thick sulfate layers. Coordinates approximate.

targets.name: Arsia Mons — cave skylights
targets.desc: Cave skylights and lava tubes on the flanks of a shield volcano; a candidate underground shelter.

targets.name: Hebrus Valles
targets.desc: Flood channels with cave openings; proposed as a human exploration zone.

targets.name: Olympus Mons
targets.desc: The tallest volcano in the Solar System; its basalt flows carry lava channels and tubes.

targets.name: Arcadia Planitia
targets.desc: Near-surface ice at mid-latitudes; a candidate human landing site. Coordinates approximate.

targets.name: Deuteronilus Mensae
targets.desc: Debris-covered glaciers — a large water source for crewed missions.

targets.name: Korolev Crater
targets.desc: An impact crater filled with a permanent water-ice mound about 1.8 km thick.

targets.name: Vastitas Borealis — Phoenix
targets.desc: Phoenix scraped water ice just below the soil and found perchlorate.

targets.name: Utopia — Viking 2
targets.desc: Northern plains with winter frost and terrain pointing to subsurface ice.

targets.name: Southern Utopia — Zhurong
targets.desc: China's rover site, near the edge of a possible ancient northern ocean.

targets.name: Chryse Planitia — Viking 1
targets.desc: Mouth of huge outflow channels; first successful Mars landing (1976).

targets.name: Ares Vallis — Pathfinder
targets.desc: A rocky plain left by ancient catastrophic floods.

targets.name: Elysium — InSight
targets.desc: A flat basalt plain chosen for landing safety, where marsquakes were recorded.

targets.name: Medusae Fossae Formation
targets.desc: The largest yardang field on Mars, carved by wind in friable deposits, and a major dust source.

targets.name: Hellas Basin
targets.desc: The deepest impact basin on Mars, with higher air pressure and frequent dust storms.

_meta.name: SameBeyond analog atlas dataset

climate_formulas.moon_mars_climate: fixed at 1.0 (extreme) for all off-world sites

_meta.score: weighted mean of (1-|site-ref|) over 13 dims; weight x2 where reference value >= 0.8
_meta.coordinates_note: Off-world lat/lon are planetocentric, east-positive, -180..180. Artemis III regions use the centre of the eponymous named feature (approximate).
